paper.title: Modal Approach to the Theory of Energy Transfer Mediated by a Metallic Nanosphere
paper.abstract: Theoretically, the presence of a metallic nanoparticle enhances the intermolecular energy transfer. We calculate this enhancement factor with a modal approach pertaining analytical results in the case of a nanosphere. We calculate the Green's function of the system relaying on the spectral properties of the electrostatic operator, fully known for spherical geometry. In contrast to other treatments, the present calculations are straightforward for any molecular orientation giving modal information about the response of the system. Numerical calculations and further discussions are also provided.

artifact_assessment.evidence: no availability statement or link in the text

flag_details.ELEVATED_SELF_CITATION: 9 of 32 references (28%) include the first author (refs 13-15, 23-26, 28, 29). Refs 13-15 (two-level systems coupled to quantum oscillators) are only marginally related to plasmon-enhanced FRET; the rest concern the same boundary-operator method.
flag_details.NO_LIMITATIONS: The paper lists limitations of Förster theory in general but not of its own model: the electrostatic (nonretarded) approximation and point-dipole treatment are stated as assumptions, never discussed as constraints. The comparison with the fully retarded results of ref. 30 is qualitative only.

verdict.summary: Analytical physics paper deriving a boundary Green's function for plasmon-enhanced FRET near a nanosphere. The formalism is the substance of the paper and is proportionate. Self-citation is elevated, own limitations are not discussed, and the numerical code is not released.

## Formalism Analysis

### Concept Complexity
**Topic:** Analytical derivation of the plasmonic enhancement factor of Förster resonance energy transfer near a metallic nanosphere, using the spectral decomposition of the surface electrostatic operator to build a boundary Green's function.
**Level:** 3 (Medium)
**Rationale:** It builds a new analytical model (Eq. 24, claimed new in the literature) by applying the authors' established operator method to a new problem. The paper has no proofs or protocol guarantees, so it does not reach Level 4.

### Formal Elements
- Definitions: 0 (formal)
- Theorems: 0
- Proofs: 0
- Equations: ~26 (Green's functions, eigenfunction expansions, interaction energy, enhancement factors)

### Proportionality
Calculated complexity: 0
Expected range (Level 3): 10-40
Ratio: 0x upper bound

**Assessment:** Proportionate. Each equation is needed for the derivation. The enhancement factors (Eqs. 25-26) cannot be computed without the spherical-harmonic expansion, so it passes the necessity test. There is no decorative notation.

### Issues
None identified in the formalism. Eq. (9) is labelled Φfree where Φbound is meant, a typographical slip.

---

## Citation Analysis

9 of 32 references include the first author (28%). Refs 23-26, 28 and 29 cover the boundary-integral eigenmode method used here, or a conference version of this work, and are relevant. Refs 13-15 (dynamic squeezing and strongly coupled two-level systems/oscillators) back a generic remark that strong fields cause strong light-matter coupling. They are only marginally related (similarity about 0.35), which is not low enough for the irrelevant-citation flag. Refs 11 and 12 are the same paper listed twice.

---

## Structural Analysis

The claims follow from the derivation. The numerical results for a Drude silver sphere are said to be "consistent" with ref. 30, but no quantitative comparison is given. The authors do not acknowledge the limits of their own model (nonretarded approximation, point dipoles, Drude parameters). One phenomenon (the common dip) is left for later work. No code or data for the numerical results is offered.

---

## Conclusion

This is a sound, compact theoretical paper whose mathematics matches its subject. Its weaknesses are a self-citation share near the 30% threshold, padded with marginally related quantum-optics work, no discussion of the model's own limits, and only qualitative validation against other calculations.

paper.title: Electro-Optical Method for Surface Recombination Evaluation in Silicon Carbide Bipolar Junction Transistors
paper.abstract: This paper reports two original methods aimed for the surface recombination studies of bipolar junction transistors made on silicon carbide subject to a significant surface recombination around the emitter-base junction. The first novel method targets the measurement of very short minority carrier lifetime in semiconductor junctions by combining the current switch lifetime measurement approach with electro-optical excitation. The second method is elaborated to evaluate individually the surface recombination velocity for each transistor using the combined electro-optical measurement of very short lifetime in base-emitter junctions. Previous to its use for silicon carbide BJTs, the first presented method was tested and calibrated on silicon bipolar transistors using combined electro-optical measurements.

artifact_assessment.evidence: no availability statement or link in the text

verdict.summary: Experimental measurement-method paper combining current-switch lifetime measurement with optical excitation to estimate base-emitter lifetime and surface recombination velocity in SiC BJTs. Its formalism is standard device physics. It has internal inconsistencies, a duplicated paragraph, and limited statistical support.

## Formalism Analysis

### Concept Complexity
**Topic:** An electro-optical measurement procedure: the ratio of photocurrent slopes of the BC and BE junctions, calibrated against the electrically measured BC lifetime, gives the effective BE lifetime and from it the surface recombination velocity.
**Level:** 2 (Low)
**Rationale:** It applies textbook p-n junction photocurrent and lifetime relations to a new measurement setup, with empirical calibration. No new theory.

### Formal Elements
- Definitions: 0
- Theorems: 0
- Proofs: 0
- Equations: 19 (storage-time relation, photocurrent, diffusion length, Einstein relation, slope ratios, lifetime and surface-recombination relations)

### Proportionality
Calculated complexity: 0
Expected range (Level 2): 0-15
Ratio: 0x upper bound

**Assessment:** Proportionate. The equations carry the derivation of the measurement principle (Eqs. 12-13, 17, 19), so they pass the necessity test. The symbols are physical quantities, not decorated configuration parameters.

### Issues
None in the formalism. The collapse of mobility and lifetime ratios into a single factor B (Eq. 6-7) is an unexamined simplifying assumption.

---

## Citation Analysis

1 of 11 references is a self-citation (ref. 1, the conference version of this work), about 9%. It is relevant. No issues identified.

---

## Structural Analysis

The Si calibration gives a mean slope ratio with standard deviations and a stated 10% accuracy, which is reasonable evidence. The SiC results rest on a few transistor versions, and there is no uncertainty analysis for the derived recombination velocities. The text has internal inconsistencies. Section 3.4 calls the mean S "6 x larger" than a literature value printed as 5×10^5 cm/s (which would make it smaller), while the conclusion gives that value as 5×10^4 cm/s. One whole paragraph is printed twice. Inline limitations appear: the authors admit they cannot explain the decreasing S versus P/A trend, and they note that BC lifetime is assumed equal to bulk lifetime. No data or analysis files are offered.

---

## Conclusion

This is a practical measurement contribution with appropriate, necessary equations and clean citation practice. Its weaknesses are presentation errors, a contradictory comparison with the literature, and thin statistical support for the SiC results.

paper.title: Assessing by Raman spectroscopy the quality of CVD graphene transferred on oxidized silicon and quartz substrates
paper.abstract: We present the results of a study regarding CVD graphene transfer from copper foil to other substrates - oxidized silicon and quartz by means of electrochemical delamination. Transfer results were examined by means of Raman spectroscopy using a laser at 633 nm and confocal optical microscopy to identify graphene in good optical contrast conditions. Characteristic Raman bands of graphene - D, G and 2D are certifying if a transfer process has been performed successfully. The quality of the transferred graphene are evidenced by the modifications in the main graphene Raman bands D, G, 2D from which quality (I2D/IG) and defect (ID/IG) ratio's were extracted. We are also highlighting critical steps in the transfer process. The final step of Polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) removal is the most critical one due to the partially folding of graphene. After transfer defects are induced in graphene which is confirmed by the increase of the ratio of the intensity of the D band to the G (ID/IG).

paper.title: Effect of Silicon Surface Cleaning on Electrical Properties of As-Deposited Atomically Layer-Deposited (ALD) HfO2 Films Obtained From Tetrakis(dimethylamino)Hafnium (TDMAH) and Water
paper.abstract: The paper presents the results of an experimental study of the electrical properties of ultrathin as-deposited HfO2 films prepared at 200°C by atomic layer deposition (ALD) from the reaction between tetrakis(dimethylamino)hafnium (TDMAH) and water as function of silicon surface terminations. The comparison of high frequency C-V plots recorded on Al-HfO2-Si MOS capacitors prepared on Si-OH and Si-H terminated silicon and thermally annealed in nitrogen at 250°C have indicated a two-fold smaller oxide trapped charge, and a 5% higher effective dielectric constant (9.95) for capacitors prepared Si-OH with respect the same capacitors processed on Si-H terminated silicon. Weibull plots of the HfO2 breakdown events at constant current injection through the dielectric as a function of charge to breakdown have revealed an increased reliability of the HfO2 films deposited on Si-OH terminated silicon substrate, in terms of a much smaller number of early breakdown events and higher capability of carrying electrical charges, before failure. The results are explained in terms of reaction mechanism between TDMAH and silicon termination and its role on interface and bulk HfO2 film properties.

paper.title: Technological aspects and simulation results for the Nothing On Insulator device developed into a planar technology
paper.abstract: This paper presents the simulations results of a planar variant of Nothing On Insulator device starting from Si-surface preparation till the fine oxide configuration of few nanometers. A dry oxidation at lower temperature is a better process to a higher temperature in a time under 1min. But the final experimental technological tests find the best solution - relatively high temperature, acceptable time of 5-8 min, but dilution of the O2 fluids in the furnace adding N2 in a suitable ratio. The functionality of the planar variant p-NOI was tested by Atlas simulations in two cases: (i) a p-NOI structure with 10nm SiO2 when it is compared to a standard simulated MOSFET from Atlas and (ii) a p-NOI structure with SiO2/HfO2 stack when it is compared with an insulator stack with similar composition of one of the lasts generation fabricated MOSFET. The conduction mechanism obeys to the Fowler-Nordheim's law. The current flow from source to drain occurs in absence of an inversion channel. A similar investigated device by other authors is a fabricated MIM (Metal-Insulator-Metal) structure, which is compared with the actual p-NOI simulation. The simulations fit over the experimental picked points from different resources.

The conclusion that the Fowler-Nordheim mechanism "was firmly demonstrated" rests only on simulations in which the FN model was switched on, which makes the argument close to circular. The paper reports work in progress on a device concept with no formalism problems. Its evidential support is weak because simulation stands in for measurement of the fabricated device, and its citation profile is dominated by the first author's own earlier NOI papers, triggering the excessive self-citation flag.

paper.title: Galvanically Isolated IGBT Gate Driver with Advanced Protections and A Fault Detection and Reporting Method
paper.abstract: This paper presents a method for detecting and reporting fault signals that can occur in the normal functionality of galvanically isolated Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistor (IGBT) gate drivers with advanced protection circuits. The method provides robust transmission of Under Voltage Lock Out (UVLO) and Desaturation (DESAT) events, while the protection methods, such as soft shutdown and Active Miller Clamp (AMC), prevent improper functionality that can damage the IGBT. The technique introduces a block that prioritizes and encodes the error signals in a manner that allows area and cost minimization, as well as reducing the power consumption of the gate driver. The proposed circuit was verified by means of simulations, and implemented in a standard 0.25µm CMOS BCD technology, as part of a galvanically isolated IGBT gate driver. Experimental results highlight proper reporting of UVLO/DESAT faults and validate the functionality of the protection functions.

## Structural Analysis

The functionality claims are backed by simulation waveforms and oscilloscope captures for each fault case, which is adequate evidence that the circuit works. paper.title: Efficiency Optimizations for Koller and Sahami's Feature Selection Algorithm
paper.abstract: This article describes and evaluates four optimizations for Koller and Sahami's Feature Selection algorithm, significantly reducing the time it requires to complete. The optimizations exploit the Information Theory concepts used by the algorithm, its inherent data parallelism and the fact that much of the calculations it performs are redundant. Each proposed optimization was carefully evaluated, showing significant efficiency gains. In particular, a decomposition of conditional mutual information is shown to reduce the time required to calculate its primary heuristic and can be potentially applied to other algorithms which calculate conditional mutual information.

artifact_assessment.evidence: "This implementation has been published online [16] under the GPL 3 license." Ref. 16: https://github.com/camilbancioiu/MBFF; data: "The documents in the dataset and their assignments to classes were extracted from the Reuters Corpus Volume 1 [15]."

flag_details.FORMALISM_THEATER: Level 2 paper (engineering optimizations of an existing algorithm: caching, multiprocessing, an entropy rewrite) containing formal elements that fail the necessity test: the set-builder definition of aMB (Eq. 4), the recursive set-difference definition of KS (Eq. 6), and the tuple 'definition' of a worker subprocess (Eq. 19). The paper itself restates Eq. 4 in plain English as 'the best subset of K features Fj from G, when sorted by the γ heuristic'.
flag_details.UNNECESSARY_SET_THEORY: Eq. 4 uses nested set-builder notation with card({...}) < K to express 'take the top K features by γ' (a sort and slice). Eq. 6 uses G_r = G_{r-1} − {F_i | argmin δ} to express 'remove the feature with the lowest δ from the list'. No proof depends on either.

verdict.summary: Engineering paper that speeds up Koller and Sahami's feature-selection algorithm through an entropy decomposition of its γ heuristic, a results database, multiprocessing, and an iteration cache. The useful entropy algebra is offset by set-builder notation for sort-and-slice and list-removal operations, which triggers the formalism-theater flags at Level 2. Code is public on GitHub and the data come from RCV1.

papers.provenance:
## Formalism Analysis

### Concept Complexity
**Topic:** Four implementation-level optimizations of the 1996 Koller-Sahami Markov-blanket feature filter: rewriting γ (conditional mutual information) as a sum of joint entropies so terms can be cached and shared, a persistent database of removed features, process-level parallelism within iterations, and an iteration cache of approximate Markov blankets. Evaluated by wall-clock time on an RCV1 subset.
**Level:** 2 (Low)
**Rationale:** These are simple optimizations of an existing method: memoization, caching and SPMD parallelism, plus an entropy identity drawn from ref. 18 and standard information theory. There is no complexity analysis or proof.

### Formal Elements
- Definitions: 0 numbered; inline formal definitions of γ, D_KL, aMB, δ, KS and subprocess
- Theorems: 0
- Proofs: 0
- Equations: 19

### Proportionality
Calculated complexity: 0 (no numbered definitions, theorems or proofs)
Expected range (Level 2): 0-15
Ratio: 0x upper bound

**Assessment:** The count is within range, but the paper fails the necessity test. Eqs. 1-3, 5, 7-18 (KL divergence, entropies, and the γ decomposition) are needed: the decomposition in Eq. 18 is the actual Gamma Decomposition optimization, and English would not convey it. Three elements fail:
- Eq. 4 defines the approximate Markov blanket with nested set-builder notation and a cardinality condition. In code this is `sorted(G - {Fi}, key=gamma)[:K]`, and the paper restates it in English immediately afterwards.
- Eq. 6 defines the algorithm recursively as G_r = G_{r-1} − {F_i | argmin δ}, a list removal inside a loop.
- Eq. 19 writes a worker process's return value as a formal tuple, which is just a function returning three values.

### Issues
Set notation stands in for sorting, slicing and list removal (Eqs. 4, 6), and a tuple notation describes a multiprocessing worker (Eq. 19). Under the Level 1-2 zero-tolerance rule these trigger FORMALISM_THEATER and UNNECESSARY_SET_THEORY.

---

## Citation Analysis

There are 2 self-references out of 18: ref. 2 (Băncioiu and Vințan, an earlier comparison using this same implementation) and ref. 16 (the authors' own GitHub repository). That is about 11%, and both are directly relevant. Refs 5 and 11 are the same paper listed twice. No issues identified.

---

## Structural Analysis

The efficiency claims are backed by per-class timing tables (Tables 1-3) and cache hit rates (Table 4). Each configuration was run once per class on a single machine, so run-to-run variance is not reported. The tests use a single dataset of 628 documents and 2645 words, and K=5 is fixed throughout. The headline 4.36% combined figure has no table of its own. Limitations are acknowledged inline: floating-point differences change the γ ordering, the iteration cache will be less effective on datasets with strongly correlated weak features, and the OS-level process mapping may be imperfect. The quality of the selected features is deliberately left to earlier work. The code is public (GPL, GitHub), and the data are a subset of the public RCV1 corpus, although the exact subset selection is not described.

---

## Conclusion

This is a useful, reproducible engineering contribution with released code and a public corpus. Its central mathematical step, the entropy decomposition of γ, is legitimate. However, the paper also writes ordinary programming operations (top-K selection, list removal, a function's return tuple) in set-theoretic notation. At concept Level 2 this is formalism theater under the framework's zero-tolerance rule, and it disqualifies the paper despite its otherwise sound evidence and strong artifact availability.
